name: Neck Skin Consistency
description: Compares neck skin texture properties such as wrinkle depth, pore density, and specular response against the face region to identify boundary discontinuities from face-only deepfake generation.
algorithm: Neck Skin Consistency — Pixel-Level Spatial Analysis
mechanism:
This method analyzes neck skin characteristics for deepfake detection:

1. **Neck Region Segmentation**: The neck region is segmented — the area between the jawline and collar/clothing line. This region is forensically important as it lies at the boundary or outside the typical face-swap region.

2. **Face-Neck Skin Matching**: Skin characteristics (color, tone, texture, sun damage, aging) should be consistent between face and neck. The method compares skin properties across the face-neck boundary. Face-swap deepfakes may show mismatched skin between the generated face and original neck — different color temperature, different texture quality, or different aging characteristics.

3. **Neck Skin Texture Analysis**: Neck skin has characteristic texture: horizontal creases (neck lines), visible platysma muscle bands in some individuals, and different pore distribution than facial skin. The method evaluates whether neck texture is consistent with the face age and quality. AI-generated faces may show an unnatural transition at the jaw-neck boundary.

4. **Color Continuity Across Jaw**: The color transition from face to neck should be smooth and physically motivated (slightly different sun exposure). The method measures color discontinuity at the jawline. Deepfake blending often creates subtle but detectable color seams at this boundary.

5. **Temporal Neck-Face Coherence**: Neck skin should respond to head motion consistently — rotating head reveals different neck surfaces, creates characteristic skin folds, and shows consistent skin tone from different angles. The method tracks neck-face coherence across frames. Deepfake face movement that doesn't correctly account for neck kinematics produces detectable inconsistencies.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through neck skin consistency analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video
